methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A regional AI readiness initiative in Roanoke Valley signals intentional capacity-building outside NoVA, potentially distributing applied AI fluency through local evaluation and deployment—though success depends on whether this yields deep capability or surface-level adoption.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's data center cancellation in NoVA due to local backlash reveals infrastructure saturation in the dominant hub, potentially redirecting AI/data center growth to secondary Virginia markets and inadvertently promoting geographic distribution.

signals.title: Data center rumors fly in Marion after town council won’t name developer interested in 200 acres of government property
signals.signal_reading: Data center speculation in Marion without transparency or community engagement suggests extractive infrastructure deployment in Southwest Virginia—capturing energy/tax benefits while bypassing local workforce development, reinforcing shallow regional participation in the AI economy.

signals.title: Lawyers need AI education, not AI legislation - Virginia Lawyers Weekly
signals.signal_reading: Legal profession's emphasis on AI education over regulation signals recognition that deep capability development, not governance frameworks alone, determines whether Virginia's professional class can distribute AI fluency across practice areas and regions.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's statewide AI cybersecurity order concentrates defensive AI capability development in Richmond's state apparatus, risking a policy-infrastructure gap where central government builds expertise while local jurisdictions lack implementation capacity.
